record_notes.DCP-LETT-341: Catherine answers an unlocated recent long Darwin letter about London, Covington wages and books. Newspaper report and family messages are embedded sources; no contemporaneous Darwin receipt witness identified here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-467: Yarrell sends an extract from Hindmarsh on Chillingham cattle. Quoted publication is incoming context, not Yarrell original observation or Darwin voice. Later Variation citation cannot backdate receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-457: Yarrell copy of a Heron letter, including Received December 17. That date may concern Heron-to-Yarrell receipt; it is not securely Darwin receipt. Keep circa date and layered authorship; later marginal references are not 1838 knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-502: Draft questions in Covington hand with Darwin corrections, not an extant final sent copy. Draft is Darwin-authored despite amanuensis. Input is Herbert book; request through Henslow and tomorrow-ten instruction do not supply a matched letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-523: Draft thanks Herbert for a long letter addressed to Henslow, then asks follow-up Hippeastrum, crocus and reversion questions. Original third-party letter remains outside the to/from-Darwin corpus. Empty quotation space must not be filled with invented text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-524: Herbert directly answers 523, including its gift and distinctive hybrid-pollen and reversion questions. Incoming-only reverse edge; no Darwin receipt inferred. Circa June27 conflicts with body Wednesday if treated as exact: June27,1839 was Thursday. Preserve uncertainty and direction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-526: Yarrell acknowledges Journal and sends British Birds. Book receipt rather than a surviving Darwin covering letter is established for Yarrell; no later Darwin letter witness here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-536: Returns a reviewed proof and thanks for a borrowed book; requests Annales Maritimes. Paper identified only probably in editorial note. No incoming cover note survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-537: Returns different proofs, acknowledges Annales order and Humboldt extract forwarded by Washington. This is not necessarily Humboldt personal letter534. Ordering action follows a request, but no incoming Washington letter is identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-544: Requests location and chart for iceberg-rock report, plus addresses for Humboldt and Krusenstern. Scientific report and address request do not establish an incoming letter prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-556: Initiates Redfield correspondence after reading his published whirlwind paper. Includes Tillard quotation; quoted third-party passage is not original Darwin observation. 565H later explicitly answers this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-565H: Explicitly acknowledges February24 Darwin letter received via Silliman a few days before May6 and promises meteorological papers and New York reports. Reverse reply to556 is secure; composition does not date Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-568: Accepts being proposed for RGS Council. Invitation medium and actual surviving text unlocated; election May25 is later than this acceptance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-585: Belatedly thanks Redfield for meteorological pamphlets and geological reports and says his letter is mislaid. Distinctive bundle and explicit letter reference support565H as the input; possible missing covering note remains a stated caveat. Actual receipt predates the December22 response by an unspecified interval.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-598A: Redfield introduces John Blunt as bearer with new geological report and tornado papers in May1841. This is later than585 and cannot be its input. Delivery is intended, not proved by composition.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-619: Read Strickland draft laws and forwarded the paper to Ogilby; written report is the object, not an extant incoming letter. Gray identity is editorially probable, not a blanket alias with G.R.Gray.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-620: Reports yesterday conversation with Andrew Smith about nomenclature. Oral source, not a letter pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-630: Reviews a corrected nomenclature report and suggests limits on renaming and authority attribution. Committee/report transmission is context; no incoming letter identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-637: Detailed Down House assessment after sleeping nearby and returning yesterday. Purchase and improvements remain prospective. Surviving body ends mid-sentence and must be treated as incomplete, not a complete letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-638: Approves additions and has signed Waterhouse list; returns an enclosure and reports his Welsh geological trip. No specific incoming letter identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-613: Declines Bicheno meeting after tiring conversation with Yarrell yesterday. Asks for written questions if needed; this is a prospective prompt, not an existing one. Two Monday alternatives retained.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-633: Discusses Down move, draft letter to Cockell for father review, bill and medicine list. Embedded Dear Sir is quotation of Darwin own draft opening. Blunt items and intended consultations are not surviving incoming letter prompts.
